review_text: The single-origin pour-over here is the best I've had in town. Cozy atmosphere, great music.
Decent coffee but the pastries were dry. Nothing special, would go elsewhere.
Absolutely love this place! The cinnamon rolls are to die for and the baristas are so friendly.
Overpriced for what you get. The latte was lukewarm and the croissant tasted stale.
Perfect spot for a quiet morning with a book. The Ethiopian roast was smooth and flavorful.
The space is nice but it gets incredibly crowded on weekends. Hard to find a seat.
Best flat white in the neighborhood, no contest. The almond croissant is a must-try.
Coffee was okay but the service was slow. Waited 15 minutes for a simple espresso.
Loved the seasonal special — a cardamom oat latte. Creative and delicious!
Not bad, but the seating is limited. Great coffee, average ambiance.
The homemade banana bread with their pour-over was the perfect combo. Will be back!
Disappointed. The 'organic' beans tasted like they were from a supermarket. Not worth the hype.
Cozy corner with a window seat is my favorite spot. The cold brew is refreshing and not too sweet.
Good coffee, but the wifi was down all afternoon. If you need to work here, check first.
The barista remembered my name and my usual order. Felt like a regular, which I loved!
Average at best. The cappuccino was too bitter and the muffin was overbaked.
Beautiful interior, great lighting for photos, and the matcha latte is surprisingly good.
Solid neighborhood cafe. Nothing groundbreaking but consistently good quality.
The single-origin Kenyan pour-over was a revelation. Bright, fruity, and perfectly brewed.
Went in expecting a chain-cafe experience. Got something better — personal, warm, and the pastries are genuinely homemade.
